summary: Troubleshoot a Getac device where ePR is running offline or has no Vodafone/cellular connectivity.
prechecks: Confirm caller is using a Getac ePR device.
Ask where the crew are (hospital, station, scene).
Ask if they can see or are connected to GovRoam.
steps: Ask crew to press the P2 button on the front of the Getac or swipe in from the right edge of the screen to open the action/notification menu.
Ask them to tap 'Network' at the bottom.
If connected to 'GovRoam', ask them to tap it and select 'Disconnect'.
Ensure 'Cellular' is turned on (highlighted/blue) and Airplane mode is OFF.
Check that the Vodafone connection is showing as connected. It may show 'No internet access' but this can be normal for ePR.
If there is no Vodafone/cellular adapter showing at all, ask the crew to restart the Getac.
If Vodafone still does not appear after a restart, log the device for rebuild or swap-out as a likely driver/modem issue.
important_notes: If connectivity is lost mid-ePR, the hospital may only see part of the record.
To ensure all data is sent, the crew must connect to a YAS network (e.g. station Wi-Fi) and relaunch the ePR client so it can sync local data.
If the crew refuse to travel to a YAS station to sync, they must rewrite the full record on paper – do not leave data stored only on the device.
escalation: If Vodafone/cellular adapter is still completely missing after reboot, arrange device swap-out/rebuild.
If several devices in the same area are affected, escalate as a possible network or infrastructure outage.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 29: Connectivity
Getac Service Desk Doc – No Connectivity

summary: Resolve issues where the Getac screen is very dim even when brightness appears to be on maximum.
prechecks: Confirm the issue is with screen brightness rather than ePR content.
Confirm the crew are using a Getac ePR device.
steps: Ask the crew to press FN + F7 on the Getac keyboard to increase brightness.
If the screen is still dim, ask the crew to carefully check both battery flaps on the left and right sides of the device.
Ask them to ensure each battery flap is fully closed with no visible gaps at any corner.
Once flaps are fully closed, recheck the screen brightness.
important_notes: Partially open battery flaps can force the device into a low-brightness mode.
The crew may think a flap is closed when there is still a small gap at one corner.
escalation: If the brightness is still low after flap checks and FN + F7, log the device for further hardware investigation or swap-out.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 3: Getac brightness

summary: Fix a Getac device that appears to have power (LEDs on) but the screen remains black.
triggers: Power lights on but no display
Screen black even though device is on
prechecks: Confirm power indicator LEDs are lit.
Confirm no visible image on the screen even after adjusting brightness.
steps: Ask the crew to power the Getac off if possible.
Ask them to remove both batteries at the same time to fully remove power from the device.
After a short pause, ask them to reinsert both batteries.
Ensure the battery flaps are fully closed on both sides with no gaps.
Ask them to power the device back on and confirm if the screen now displays normally.
important_notes: This procedure fully power-cycles the Getac and often resolves display lockups.
Battery flaps not closing properly can also affect brightness and display behaviour.
escalation: If the screen is still black after a full power cycle, log the device for swap-out as a likely hardware failure.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 15: Lights on Getac but screen black

summary: Troubleshoot a Getac that is not charging or powering on when placed in a vehicle dock.
triggers: Getac power issue on vehicle dock
prechecks: Confirm the vehicle ignition is switched on.
Ask if the crew can see a green LED lit on the power pack at the rear of the dock.
steps: Ask the crew to ensure the Getac is closed before docking.
Ask them to seat the Getac on the lower dock hooks and then push it firmly against the back plate of the dock.
Wait 1–2 seconds to see if the charging LED on the Getac illuminates before closing the retaining clip.
If the LED does not light, ask them to slightly move the Getac up against the dock back plate to help it align with the locating pins.
If possible, ask them to try the same Getac on another known-good dock in a different vehicle.
If the Getac charges on another dock, the original dock is faulty.
If the Getac does not charge on any dock, treat the Getac as the likely fault.
important_notes: New style Getac devices will only dock into the newer dock design; they are not compatible with old-style docks.
Until the hardware is fixed, the crew should use paper documentation and inform their Clinical Supervisor.
escalation: If the dock is faulty: advise the crew to use paper, inform the Clinical Supervisor, arrange for the vehicle to attend Fleet, log a ticket with call sign and station, and email the Fleet and Estates helpdesk with details.
If the Getac itself is faulty across multiple docks: add the device to the swap-out process.
source: Getac Service Desk Doc – Dock issue
Guide for ePR oncall – Section 17: Dock issue

subcategory: ePR not displaying / ALT+TAB warning boxes
summary: Handle cases where ePR is not visible or appears to crash on finalising due to hidden warning boxes.
prechecks: Confirm the crew can still see the Windows launcher or desktop.
Confirm whether the crash happens when they click 'relaunch ePR' after finalising.
steps: Ask the crew to press ALT + TAB to cycle through open windows.
If any ePR warning boxes are visible, ask them to click 'OK' on each one until they are all closed.
Explain that these warning boxes cause ePR to crash when finalising and relaunching.
If there are multiple warning boxes or you cannot remote in to help, ask the crew to restart the Getac to clear any stuck processes.
important_notes: Finalising of the ePR record itself typically still completes; the crash affects the relaunch step.
ALT+TAB warning boxes usually appear when ePR is already open and the crew click the ePR button on the launcher again, or when a previous crash did not close cleanly.
escalation: If ePR continues to crash after clearing warning boxes and a full restart, consider recreating the local database and investigate further.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 2: ePR not displaying - ALT and TAB

subcategory: ePR running slow – recreate local database
summary: Improve performance by recreating the local ePR database on a Getac.
prechecks: Confirm that the crew have completed and finalised any ePRs they need on this device.
Confirm that the ePR client is fully closed on the device.
Explain that recreating the database means they will not be able to access any in-progress ePR that has not been finalised.
steps: From your machine, open File Explorer and connect to the device using \\getacname\C$ or \\IPaddress\C$.
Navigate to 'Users' > 'EPR' > 'AppData'.
If 'AppData' is not visible, enable 'Hidden items' in the View menu.
Go to 'Local' > 'Apps' > '2.0'.
Open the non-'data' folder with the 'strange name', then open the most recent 'epr...tion' folder.
Open the 'DataOp' folder.
Locate 'ePCRLocalV1.db3' and rename it to '_ePCRLocalV1.db3'.
Confirm that any 'ePCRLocalV1.db3-shm' or 'ePCRLocalV1.db3-wal' files are not present or indicate that ePR is closed.
Ask the crew to relaunch ePR from the launcher. A new database will be created automatically.
important_notes: Folders beginning 'ePCRLocalV1-<number>-GUID-BAK' are historical databases for individual ePRs once data has synced to the server.
The 'ePCRLocalLookups' file controls local lookups such as crew data, hospital destinations, departments, drug names and routes.
If the ePCRLocalLookups file is unusually small or missing, it can prevent certain data from populating in the client; replacing it with a known-good copy can help.
Never open the live database while ePR is running as this can lock the client and create audit exceptions; copy it elsewhere for viewing if necessary.
escalation: If recreating the database does not improve performance, consider recreating the full local EPR profile on the device.
If problems persist after profile recreation, log for rebuild or further 2nd line investigation.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 13: Recreate a database / ePR running slow

summary: Recreate the full EPR local Windows profile on a Getac when performance issues persist after recreating the database.
triggers: ePR still running slow after database recreation
prechecks: Confirm that recreating the local database has already been attempted.
Ensure that the caller understands this is an advanced action and that the configuration steps will be required afterwards.
steps: On the EPR launcher, click 'Restart' and then 'No' so 'Restart' is highlighted.
Press and hold ALT, then press F11 to reveal the Windows taskbar.
Open the Start menu and sign out of the EPR local account.
Sign into an admin account (e.g. 'administrator' or other IT admin account).
Open 'This PC' properties and select 'Advanced system settings'.
Under the 'Advanced' tab, in 'User Profiles', click 'Settings'.
Select the '/EPR' user profile and click 'Delete'.
Restart the Getac until it logs back into the EPR local account (this may take several reboots).
Once logged in as EPR local, reinstall the relevant EPR client (e.g. Live) using the appropriate installer link.

Clean up the UI: remove pinned apps from the taskbar, adjust quick actions to only show Network, unpin unnecessary Start menu tiles, disable the touchscreen keyboard auto-popup, and hide desktop icons as per standard build.
Check and enable spellcheck following the spellcheck procedure if required.
important_notes: This action effectively recreates the EPR local Windows profile and should only be performed by appropriate support staff.
After profile recreation, the device needs to be reconfigured to match the standard YAS EPR build.
escalation: If performance or profile issues persist after recreation, log the device for a full rebuild or escalated 2nd line investigation.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 14: Recreate a profile – ePR running slow after database recreated

summary: Process when crews realise they have forgotten to add information or need to correct details on an ePR.
triggers: Crew forgot to enter some information
Need to correct details on the ePR
prechecks: Confirm whether the ePR is an accepted transfer or not.
Obtain the incident number and PCRID.
steps: If the record is an accepted transfer:
- Ask the crew to email yas.epramendments@nhs.net including the incident number, PCRID and the details that need amending.
- Remind the crew to inform the receiving hospital of any changes and to log a Datix if appropriate.
If the ePR is NOT a transfer:
- Ask the crew to create a second ePR using the same incident number while you are on the call so you can see it on the admin portal.
- They must complete the Incident screen, Patient screen and Patient Outcome screen.

- If the patient was transported, the original ePR will already contain pre-alert and handover details; in the new ePR they can select 'Pre-alert not required' and self-handover to allow finalisation.
- Once the second ePR is complete, link the first and second records together using the standard linking process.
important_notes: The linking process makes both records visible at the hospital and ensures a complete combined record.
Always make sure the correct records are being linked by confirming patient details.
escalation: If there is any uncertainty about which records belong to which patient, do not link and escalate to the systems team for review.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 4: ePR Amendments – missing / incorrect details on ePR

subcategory: Linking two ePRs (failed transfer or amendment)
summary: Link multiple ePRs for the same patient and incident when transfers fail or amendments have been created.
triggers: Two ePRs for the same incident
Need to link amendment record to original
prechecks: Obtain the incident number.
Confirm that both ePRs relate to the same patient by checking name and callsign.
Check the status of both records in the ePR Viewer.
steps: Open the ePR Admin portal at http://swkyasiis03.yas.nhs.uk/Live/ePRAdmin/.
From the menu, select 'ePR viewer' and then 'ePR Viewer'.
Search using the incident number.
Identify the records for the same patient (check name and callsign).
Check the 'Status' column. If one record is 'Transferred – Waiting' and the other is 'In progress' or 'Finalised', they require linking.
Note both PCRIDs, identifying which is the first record (earliest) and which is the second (latest).
From the menu, select 'Administration' then 'Link record'.
Enter the first PCRID in the top box and the second PCRID in the bottom box, then click 'Link records'.
Confirm that a message appears confirming the records are now linked.
Return to the ePR Viewer and re-search the incident to confirm that the first ePR now shows as 'Transferred' and the second shows an appropriate accepted transfer status.
important_notes: Linking records makes them immediately visible on the hospital portal, so it is critical that only correct matches are linked.
Patient name or incident numbers may contain minor errors, so always confirm details with the crew if unsure.
escalation: If there is any uncertainty about record ownership or linking fails repeatedly, escalate to the systems team.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 5: Linking ePRs (failed transfers or amendments)

subcategory: Un-transfer an ePR (2nd crew have no Getac)
summary: Un-transfer an ePR so it can be finalised and assigned directly to a hospital when the second crew have no Getac device.
triggers: Need record sending to hospital without second crew editing
prechecks: Confirm why the second crew cannot complete their own ePR (e.g. no device, swap-out, private provider).
Advise that the preferred approach is for the attending crew to complete an ePR for handover.
Record details on the on-call sheet for audit (incident number, PCRID, reason).
steps: Open the ePR Admin portal at http://swkyasiis03.yas.nhs.uk/Live/ePRAdmin/.
Open 'ePR viewer' and then 'ePR Viewer'.
Search for the incident number and locate the transfer record that shows 'Transferred – waiting'.
Note the PCRID of this record.
Go to 'Administration' then 'Link record'.
In the first box, enter the PCRID of the record to be un-transferred.
In the second box, enter '0'.
Click 'Link records'.
Confirm that the success message appears.
Return to the ePR Viewer and check that the record now shows as 'In progress'.
Go to 'Administration' > 'ePR Admin', search by Incident or PCRID, and click 'Finalise'.
Select an appropriate reason for finalisation and click 'Finalise PCR'.
Once finalised, click 'Assign', select the correct destination hospital and reason, and click 'Assign PCR'.
important_notes: Un-transferring and finalising an ePR without second crew input should be the exception, not the routine process.
All such actions should be clearly documented for audit.
escalation: If finalisation or assignment fails consistently despite browser restarts, escalate to the systems team.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 6: Un-transfer an ePR (2nd crew have no Getac)

summary: Resolve cases where a crew cannot finalise an ePR after documenting a patient refusal.
triggers: Patient refused but record will not finalise
Refusal documented but 'Finalise' button not available
prechecks: Confirm the crew are dealing with a refusal scenario.
Ask which sections of the Patient Outcome screen they have completed.
steps: Explain that marking refusal only against 'Examination' is not enough for finalisation.
Ask the crew to open the Patient Outcome section.
Check that the Patient Outcome screen is fully completed, including whether the patient was transported or not.
Ask them to select 'Transfer to hospital / treatment centre' in the outcome options. For refusal cases this will automatically mark the record as 'Not transported'.
Ensure all mandatory fields are complete.
Ask them to attempt to finalise the record again.
important_notes: The system is designed so that refusal can coexist with potential transport, which is why the outcome must still be set.
Once outcome and mandatory fields are complete, finalisation should be possible.
escalation: If finalisation still fails despite all sections being complete, consider finalising via the Admin Portal after confirming all checks, or escalate to systems.
source: Getac Service Desk Doc – Unable to finalise record when patient has refused

subcategory: Finalising an ePR via Admin Portal
summary: Use the Admin Portal to finalise an ePR when the crew cannot, after confirming all necessary sections are complete.
triggers: Crew unable to finalise despite completing everything
Request to finalise via admin portal
prechecks: Confirm that the Patient Outcome section is fully completed, including transport status and working impression.
For transported patients, confirm that the Pre-alert / Hospital handover screen is completed.
Check whether any electronic referrals (Social Care, Safeguarding adult/child) are started but not submitted; these must be submitted or cancelled.
steps: Open the ePR Admin portal at http://swkyasiis03.yas.nhs.uk/Live/ePRAdmin/.
From 'Administration', select 'ePR Admin'.
Search using the Incident number or PCRID and confirm the correct record has been located.
Click the 'Finalise' button.
Choose an appropriate reason from the 'Specify reason' dropdown.
Click 'Finalise PCR'.
Check for a success message indicating the record has been finalised.
important_notes: Do NOT finalise an ePR simply because a hospital phones and requests it. There can be unsynced data, and doing so may create conflicting versions of the truth.
Always check that all sections are appropriately complete before finalising on behalf of the crew.
escalation: If finalisation fails more than once, try closing and reopening the browser and repeating the steps.
If issues persist, escalate to the systems team.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 7: Finalising an ePR – CREW ONLY
Guide for ePR oncall – Section 21: Hospitals requesting ePRs to be finalised

subcategory: Cancelling an ePR via Admin Portal
summary: Cancel an ePR via the Admin Portal when requested by a crew and it is safe to do so.
triggers: Crew request to cancel an ePR
prechecks: Check whether the ePR contains a submitted Electronic Referral (Social Care Assessment, Safeguarding Adult, Safeguarding Child).
If there is a submitted referral, the crew should complete, not cancel, the ePR.
steps: Open the ePR Admin portal at http://swkyasiis03.yas.nhs.uk/Live/ePRAdmin/.
From 'Administration', select 'ePR Admin'.
Search using the Incident number or PCRID and confirm the correct record.
Click the 'Cancel' button.
Choose an appropriate reason from the 'Specify reason' dropdown.
Click 'Cancel PCR'.
Check for a success message indicating the record has been cancelled.
important_notes: An ePR should not be cancelled at the request of a hospital; this process is crew-driven and must respect safeguarding and referral processes.
escalation: If cancellation fails after retrying, escalate to the systems team.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 8: Cancelling an ePR – CREW ONLY

subcategory: Create new hospital user for ePR dashboard
summary: Create a new hospital user account for the ePR hospital dashboard.
triggers: New hospital staff member needs ePR dashboard access
Request to create hospital portal user
prechecks: Confirm the caller is authorised to request a new account for their hospital.
Identify the correct hospital site code.
steps: Open the ePR Admin portal at http://swkyasiis03/Live/ePRAdmin/.
From the main menu, click 'Administration', then 'User Administration'.
Click 'Add User' to create a new account.
Enter the Forename and Surname.
Enter a User ID, typically in the format firstname.surname, following existing naming conventions for that hospital.
Enter the email address if available.
Set the Site Name using the appropriate hospital code (e.g. LGI, STJ, YDH, etc.).
Tick the EPCR checkbox.
Set the initial password according to local policy (commonly 'Yasepr1' unless policy has changed).
Save the new user and arrange for the credentials to be sent securely to the hospital contact.
important_notes: Site Name must match one of the configured hospital codes for access to work correctly.
Passwords and account details should be sent using secure, approved communication channels only.
escalation: If the site code is missing or invalid, escalate to systems for configuration.
If user creation fails, capture any error messages and escalate.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 18: Create new users for hospitals

summary: Add a new non-YAS user to the ePCR portal using the self-service process.
triggers: Hospital staff require ePCR portal access
prechecks: Confirm the requester is authorised for that hospital/site.
Determine the correct hospital site code from the site list.
steps: Open the EPR admin portal at http://epradminlive.yas.nhs.uk/.
Click 'Administration', then 'Add User'.
Enter the user's first name and last name.
Enter the user's email address.
Define a username based on the format used for that hospital (check existing accounts for consistency).
Enter the appropriate site code from the site list (e.g. LGI, STJ, YDH, etc.).
Generate a strong password using an approved password generator and enter it.
Select the roles the user needs. For standard hospital A&E staff, select 'Dashboard Queues' and 'Search / View EPR'.
Click 'Add User' to create the account.
Send the username and password to the user via an approved secure method.
important_notes: Usernames and site codes must follow local conventions to avoid confusion and access issues.
The chosen roles must align with the user’s responsibilities and least-privilege principles.
escalation: If the system rejects the site code or user creation fails, escalate to the systems team with full details.
source: New User account process for ePCR Portal for non-YAS users
ePCR Portal Password reset for non-YAS users

subcategory: Reset password for non-YAS portal user
summary: Reset the password for an existing non-YAS ePCR portal user.
triggers: Non-YAS portal user has forgotten password
Account still active but password reset required
prechecks: Confirm the identity and authorisation of the requester.
Confirm the account is for a non-YAS hospital user.
steps: Open the ePR Admin portal at http://epradminlive.yas.nhs.uk/.
Click 'Administration' and then 'Manage Users'.
Filter by hospital using the drop-down and click 'Filter by hospital'.
Filter by username using the relevant drop-down and click 'Filter by username'.
Locate the user's account and click 'Edit'.
Click the 'Change Password' button.
Generate a new strong password using an approved password generator.
Enter the new password and save the changes.
Send the new password to the user via an approved secure method.
important_notes: Ensure you are resetting the correct user account, especially where naming conventions are similar.
Do not send passwords via insecure channels.
escalation: If the user cannot be found or the change fails, escalate to the systems team for further investigation.
source: ePCR Portal Password reset for non-YAS users

summary: Access an ePR via the Universal Receipt portal using the three passcodes provided by the crew.
triggers: Hospital has three passcodes from crew
Need to view ePR quickly without full portal login
prechecks: Confirm the hospital staff member has three passcodes from the crew.
Confirm the passcodes were generated within the last 24 hours.
steps: Ask the hospital user to go to https://eprweb.yas.nhs.uk/Live/dashv3/ur.
On the Universal Receipt page, ask them to enter the three passcodes provided by the ambulance crew.
Submit the passcodes to retrieve the associated ePR information.
important_notes: Universal Receipt passcodes are unique to the job and only valid for 24 hours from generation in the Patient Outcome screen.
This method does not require a named user account for access.
escalation: If the passcodes do not work and are confirmed correct and in-date, escalate to the systems team with incident details.
source: Universal Receipt – How to access universal receipt

summary: Fix spellcheck issues on the Getac ePR device by adjusting language settings.
triggers: Red underline not appearing under misspelled words
prechecks: Confirm the issue is with spellcheck and not general text entry.
Ensure the device is logged into the local EPR account.
steps: Ask the crew to power on the Getac and log into the local EPR account.
On the launcher screen, click 'Restart' and then 'No' so the restart button is highlighted.
Ask them to press ALT + F11 to show the Windows taskbar.
Ask them to open the Start menu and search for 'Settings'.
In Settings, go to 'Time & Language' then 'Language & keyboard options'.
Add a preferred language and choose 'English (United States)'.
Click 'Next' and then 'Install' (they do not need to set it as display language).
Wait for the US language pack to install; a red status text may appear while it installs.
Once installed, test spellcheck by typing a test word such as 'epr ' and checking for the red underline after a space.

If English (United States) has become the display language and the keyboard layout is now US (" and @ swapped), remove the English (United States) language pack, restart the Getac, then reinstall it ensuring UK remains the display/keyboard language.
important_notes: The aim is to enable spellcheck functionality without permanently switching the keyboard to a US layout.
Crew may need guidance to avoid accidentally making US the display language.
escalation: If spellcheck still does not work after this procedure, recreate the local profile or escalate to systems.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 31: Spellcheck issues
Getac Service Desk Doc – Spellchecker

subcategory: Screen resolution incorrect (parts of ePR missing)
summary: Correct the screen resolution on a Getac when parts of the ePR or launcher are missing or misaligned.
triggers: Cannot see handover destination or signature boxes
prechecks: Confirm the device is a Getac with ePR installed.
Confirm the user is reporting missing UI elements rather than data issues.
steps: Explain that ePR is designed to display at 1366 x 768 resolution and higher resolutions can hide elements.
On the launcher, click 'Restart' and then 'No' so restart is highlighted.
Ask the user to press and hold ALT, then press F11 to reveal the Windows taskbar.
Right-click the taskbar and choose to show the desktop.
Right-click on the desktop and select 'Display settings'.
In Display settings, select the resolution 1366 x 768 from the dropdown.
Apply the new resolution.
Restart the Getac. If the crew are in an ePR at the time, ask them to save first and then use crash recovery after reboot to avoid losing data.
important_notes: Windows may recommend 1920 x 1080, but ePR is built for 1366 x 768 to ensure all controls are visible.
Changing resolution may temporarily affect layout until rebooted.
escalation: If resolution repeatedly changes or cannot be set to 1366 x 768, log the device for further investigation.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 20: Screen resolution

summary: Troubleshoot safeguarding or social care referrals that will not submit from within ePR.
triggers: Submit to clinical hub not working
prechecks: Confirm the crew have connectivity and are not connected to GovRoam.
Confirm which type of referral they are completing (Safeguarding adult, Safeguarding child, Social care assessment).
steps: Ask the crew to check all mandatory fields in the referral. Incomplete mandatory sections are shown in pink; all sections should be grey or green.
Ensure sections such as GP, Risks and other mandatory details are populated.
If all mandatory fields are complete and it still will not submit:
- Remote onto the Getac (e.g. via DameWare) and note the referral type and the PCRID from the section selector.
- Task manager the ePR client to close it down.
- Connect to the device C drive (\\getacname\C$) and copy 'ePCRLocalV1' to your own machine.
- Open 'ePCRLocalV1' using SQLite on your machine and go to 'Browse Data'.
- In the table dropdown, choose the appropriate table:
* 'PatientOutcomeSga' for Safeguarding Adult
* 'PatientOutcomeSgc' for Safeguarding Child
* 'PatientOutcomeSca' for Social Care Assessment
- Locate the relevant row where PCRID is '0' and update the PCRID field to the correct PCRID.
- Click 'Apply' and 'Write changes'.
- Close SQLite and copy the updated local database back to the Getac C drive, overwriting the existing file.
- Ask the crew to reopen the ePR client, navigate back to the referral and attempt to submit again.
important_notes: This issue can occur when the referral record in the local database does not have the correct PCRID.
Always ensure ePR is closed before editing the local database, and work on a copy rather than the live file where possible.
escalation: If the referral still does not submit after correcting the PCRID and connectivity is confirmed, escalate to the systems team.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 28: Safeguarding referral not submitting

summary: Describe how crews should manage ePR documentation when CAD is down and incident details do not pull through.
triggers: Incident details not pulling into ePR
prechecks: Confirm there is known or suspected CAD downtime.
Confirm the crew understands that CAD-linked population of incident data will not work.
steps: Advise crews not to revert to paper purely because CAD is down; they should continue to use ePR.
Ask crews to manually enter Incident and Patient details in the ePR, as they would if they had no connectivity.
Explain that when EOC are on paper, the incident number format is Day, Month and a three-digit number from EOC.
Example: if CAD is down on 3rd September and the incident number is 001, the incident number should be entered as 0309001.
important_notes: Manual entry during CAD downtime ensures continuity of ePR use and electronic data capture.
Crew should be made aware of the correct incident number format to avoid confusion.
escalation: If CAD downtime behaviour appears inconsistent or multiple crews cannot work as described, confirm with EOC and IT whether there are wider issues.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 34: CAD downtime

summary: Troubleshoot issues where the NHS number search in ePR does not return expected results.
triggers: NHS number search not returning results
Crew believes NHS number search is broken
prechecks: Confirm the crew have connectivity; NHS number search relies on a third-party service.
Ask the crew to confirm that all required fields for the search are being completed.
steps: Remind the crew that all details in the NHS number search panel must be completed.
Ensure there are no trailing spaces at the end of names.
Ensure the postcode has a space in the correct place (e.g. 'WF8 2DH').
Ask the crew to retry the search after correcting any formatting issues.
If they still report no results, advise them to continue completing the ePR as normal and note any NHS number if obtained later.
If you want to test the service, use a test call on ePR Live with your own details, ensuring the ePR is then cancelled.
If repeated tests with known-good data fail to return results over time, escalate to the systems team.
important_notes: NHS number search is a third-party integration; connectivity is essential.
Input formatting errors (spaces, missing fields) commonly cause failed searches.
escalation: If multiple users report similar issues and tests confirm a problem, escalate to systems with times, user details and test examples.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 33: NHS number search

subcategory: Tracking a missing Getac with Absolute Software
summary: Use Absolute Software to track the last known location of a Getac device.
triggers: Getac reported lost, stolen or missing
prechecks: Obtain the full Getac device name (e.g. GTCTX08190).
Confirm the device has been powered on for at least 15 minutes recently, if possible.
steps: Access the Absolute tracking portal at https://signin.absolute.com/ using your credentials.
Once signed in, go to 'Reports' on the left-hand side.
Select the 'Last known location' report.
Accept any geolocation tracking agreement presented.
In the filters, choose 'All devices' and set the field to 'Device name'.
Enter the full Getac name in the field or choose it from the device list.
Click 'Show results'.
Review the map to see the device's last known location.
important_notes: The device must have been powered on and connected long enough for a location ping; otherwise only the last known location will be shown.
Location data should be handled according to local information governance and security policies.
escalation: If the device cannot be located or is confirmed stolen, follow local security incident and data protection procedures.
source: Guide for ePR oncall – Section 30: Absolute Software
